description: Almost no other purchase requires agreeing before the cost is knowable. Treatment is agreed to first and priced afterwards.
energy_note: Signing for an amount nobody will state.

aspect: You did not choose the providers
description: The anaesthetist, the radiologist and the lab attached to your in-network hospital may each bill separately and may each be out of network.
energy_note: Billed by people you never met, at a hospital you did choose.

aspect: The bill arrives in pieces, for months
description: Facility, physician, imaging, pathology, follow-up - separate envelopes over half a year, so you never know when it is finished.
energy_note: No way to know whether it is over.

description: One night in hospital. Over the next five months: four bills from four entities, two of which he has to phone to understand, and one that turns out to duplicate another.

aspect: Prior authorisation is a delay with a clinical cost
description: A treatment the doctor has prescribed waits for an insurer's administrative decision, which takes weeks and can be refused.
energy_note: Your clinician overruled by an administrator.

aspect: Appealing a denial is unpaid work while ill
description: Denials are appealable, and the appeal is assembled by the patient - records, letters, calls - during the illness.

aspect: Being insured does not end it
description: Deductibles, coinsurance, caps and network rules mean a covered event still produces a substantial personal bill.
energy_note: Insured, and still paying for years.

description: In most systems dental and optical are separate, so a crown or a root canal becomes a clinical need decided on affordability.
